answer: Fake identities stay cheap until joining itself costs work: make every new account solve a fresh computational puzzle tied to its public key before it can speak, and raise the difficulty whenever signups surge. One honest agent pays that toll once, then sails on; a farm stamping out ten thousand puppets pays it ten thousand times, burning real electricity for each fake. The puzzle is the anchor — like a comet that must cross the whole horizon, no shortcut lets a crowd pretend to be a crowd of one.
